$comment: Machine-readable catalog of prompt-relevant @miragon/mcp-toolkit-ui building blocks. Hand-maintained, source of truth is packages/ui/src/. A Vitest drift-guard (src/ui-catalog.test.ts) asserts every `export` named here is actually exported from its `importPath` barrel, so this file cannot silently drift from the code. Consumed by the docs/reference/components.md page and the build-mcp-widget skill. Versioned by the @miragon/mcp-toolkit-ui tarball it ships in — it carries no version field of its own. `importPath` is one of: '@miragon/mcp-toolkit-ui' (root barrel, mcp-use/react-free), '@miragon/mcp-toolkit-ui/app' (MCP app shell, imports mcp-use/react), '@miragon/mcp-toolkit-ui/hooks' (view-tool hooks).

components.name: Card

props.name: size
props.description: Compact spacing when 'sm'. Default 'default'.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root div via cn().

components.whenToUse: The default container for any widget. Compose CardHeader/CardTitle/CardContent/CardFooter instead of building a bordered div by hand.

components.name: Badge

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style. Default 'default'. danger/success/warning/info follow the tone model: tint + foreground text, rim in the tone (TONE_SOFT + TONE_BORDER). 'destructive' is the deprecated name of 'danger'.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the badge.

components.whenToUse: Inline status/label pill. For a tone-driven status dot or count, see LivePill/CountPill.

components.name: Button

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style. Default 'default'.

props.name: size
props.description: Size token. Default 'default'.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render the single child as the button (Radix Slot) instead of a <button>.

props.name: ...buttonProps
props.description: onClick, disabled, aria-*, etc.

components.whenToUse: Any clickable action. Wire onClick to a host action (useHostBridge / useHostActions) or a mutation.

components.name: Input

props.name: ...inputProps
props.description: value, onChange, placeholder, type, etc.

components.whenToUse: Single-line text/number entry in interactive widgets.

components.name: Select

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Selection callback.

components.whenToUse: Pick one option from a list (e.g. a scope/period filter that drives a self-fetch).

components.name: Switch

props.name: checked
props.description: Controlled on/off state.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Toggle callback.

components.whenToUse: Boolean toggle (e.g. include-resolved, live-refresh).

components.name: Table
components.whenToUse: Tabular markup. Compose the parts for a list/array tool result; add a ListFooter for pagination.

components.name: Tabs

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initially active tab value.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled active tab.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Active-tab callback.

components.whenToUse: Split a busy widget into sections (e.g. one tab per process key). The WidgetRenderer also uses Tabs for tabbed layouts.

components.name: Dialog

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Open-state callback.

components.whenToUse: Confirm a destructive action or show detail in a modal.

components.name: Sheet

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Open-state callback.

components.whenToUse: Slide-in side panel for detail/edit without leaving the widget.

components.name: Alert

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style. 'danger': tint, rim and icon in the danger colour, foreground text. 'destructive' is its deprecated name. For a failed fetch prefer ErrorState (title, next step, Details, retry).

components.whenToUse: Inline notice or error message inside a widget body.

components.name: ScrollArea
components.whenToUse: Constrain a long list to a fixed height with a styled scrollbar.

components.name: Skeleton

props.name: className
props.description: Size the placeholder (e.g. 'h-20 w-full').

components.whenToUse: Loading placeholder while a self-fetch is in flight — avoids layout shift on first paint.

components.name: Separator

props.name: orientation
props.description: Default 'horizontal'.

components.whenToUse: Visual divider between sections of a card.

components.name: GridLayout

props.name: children
props.description: GridItem children.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the grid container (e.g. to change the gap).

components.whenToUse: Lay out KPI tiles / sub-cards in a 12-column responsive grid. Wrap each cell in <GridItem span={n}>. Same grid WidgetRenderer uses internally.

components.name: GridItem

props.name: span
props.description: Column span 1–12. Default 12 (full width); out-of-range falls back to full width.

props.name: children
props.description: Cell content.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the cell.

components.whenToUse: A cell inside GridLayout. e.g. <GridItem span={4}> for a one-third-width tile.

components.name: KpiGrid

props.name: cells
props.description: Metric cells: { label, value, fraction?, trend?, trendDirection?: 'up'|'down'|'flat', trendTone?, tone?, onClick?, actionHint? }. Flows 1–6 columns (4+ fall back to 2 in narrow frames). A cell with onClick is a button named by its visible label and value; actionHint ('Opens the incidents dashboard') becomes its aria-describedby. ariaLabel is deprecated (it hides the visible label from voice control, WCAG 2.5.3).

props.name: variant
props.description: 'strip' (default): one bordered strip, tone as a dot next to the label. 'soft': a card per cell in its tone's tint and edge (boxed/header don't apply).

props.name: boxed
props.description: Wrap the strip in a bordered card with an optional header. Default false (lighter border-y strip).

props.name: header
props.description: Group header above the strip: { label, badge? } (13 px semibold, normal case).

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Names the group of metrics (role=group); omit when a heading right above names it.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element.

components.whenToUse: Show a row of headline metrics in a widget (replaces the old single-metric KPICard). Pre-format values for locale/currency. Figures stay in the foreground at the page-title size; a cell tone shows as a dot next to its label, a trend as a Lucide direction icon (or a dot with trendTone) next to neutral words. Set onClick + actionHint to make a metric a drill target. Pair with KpiGridSkeleton while loading.

components.name: KpiGridSkeleton

props.name: cells
props.description: How many cells the loaded grid will have.

props.name: variant
props.description: The loaded grid's variant. Default 'strip'.

props.name: boxed
props.description: The loaded grid's boxed. Default false.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element.

components.whenToUse: Loading placeholder with KpiGrid's geometry (same wrapper, grid and cell padding), so the layout doesn't jump when the data arrives. Marked aria-busy.

components.name: LivePill

props.name: tone
props.description: Status tone driving the dot, tint and border ('neutral'|'info'|'success'|'warning'|'danger'): tint + foreground text, rim in the tone (TONE_SOFT + TONE_BORDER). Default 'info'.

props.name: children
props.description: Pill label. Defaults to 'Live'.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element.

components.whenToUse: Signal live/real-time data in a widget header — a tinted pill with a pulsing dot.

components.name: CountPill

props.name: tone
props.description: Status tone driving the tint and border: tint + foreground text, rim in the tone (TONE_SOFT + TONE_BORDER); the number never takes a tone colour, also on the neutral tint. Default 'neutral'.

props.name: children
props.description: The count/value (rendered with tabular numbers).

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element.

components.whenToUse: Right-aligned count indicator on a list/group row (e.g. a per-group item count).

components.name: StatusBadge

props.name: children
props.description: The state in words ('Suspended', '3 open incidents'). Required: colour is never the only signal.

props.name: tone
props.description: The state's tone: tint, edge and a static dot ('danger'|'warning'|'success'|'info'|'neutral'; retired names map through resolveTone).

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element.

components.whenToUse: Say a state in words, marked in its tone: a detail-page header (WidgetHeader badge) or a table cell. Foreground text on the tint, never coloured words. For live data use LivePill, for a count CountPill.

components.name: SectionHeading

props.name: title
props.description: The section title.

props.name: hint
props.description: Muted hint shown on the right (e.g. a count).

props.name: trailing
props.description: Right-aligned slot that overrides hint when set (e.g. a control).

components.whenToUse: Label a block inside a widget body (a list or sub-table) without the weight of a full card header.

components.name: WidgetHeader

props.name: title
props.description: The widget title.

props.name: as
props.description: Heading element. Default 'h1'. Pick the level that keeps one outline per view: below a toolbar title (an h2) use 'h3'. The size follows `size`, not the level.

props.name: size
props.description: 'default': page title (28 px / 700); 'detail': compact detail-page title (21 px / 600).

props.name: badge
props.description: Above the title: a StatusBadge that says the state in words.

props.name: titleSuffix
props.description: Inline after the title inside the heading (e.g. a version chip).

props.name: sub
props.description: Subtitle/meta row under the title (e.g. a LivePill + counts).

props.name: actions
props.description: Right-aligned actions slot (buttons, drill controls).

props.name: icon
props.description: Deprecated: the icon tile above the title is the anti-slop U2 pattern; use badge. Still rendered (aria-hidden).

props.name: iconTone
props.description: Deprecated: tone of the icon tile.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element.

components.whenToUse: Anchor the top of a widget surface: optional state badge, the title at a configurable heading level, a meta row and an actions slot. Use once per widget; with McpAppView's toolbar title shown, set titleMode='hide' or as='h3' so the view keeps one title and one outline.

components.name: GroupCard

props.name: expanded
props.description: Whether the body is expanded.

props.name: onToggle
props.description: Toggle handler for the summary bar.

props.name: summary
props.description: Always-visible summary bar (may contain its own buttons/links; clicks on those don't toggle).

props.name: children
props.description: Collapsible body, rendered only when expanded.

components.whenToUse: Group related rows behind an expandable header (e.g. items grouped by a key). Replaces a hand-rolled Collapsible for list grouping.

components.name: FilterBar

props.name: search
props.description: Current search text (controlled).

props.name: onSearchChange
props.description: Called with the new search text on every keystroke.

props.name: chips
props.description: Toggle chips: { id, label, count?, active? }. Each is a button with aria-pressed; an active chip is the info tint and edge around foreground text.

props.name: onChipToggle
props.description: Called with a chip id when it is toggled.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.description: Placeholder for the search input. Default 'Filter…'.

props.name: searchAriaLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the search input. Default: the locale's 'Filter' (a placeholder is no label).

props.name: chipsAriaLabel
props.description: Names the chip group (role=group). Default: the locale's 'Filters'.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element.

components.whenToUse: Filter a list/table of widget items with a labelled search box + a row of toggle chips (aria-pressed). Pair with useDebouncedValue so a server-side filter only re-queries once typing pauses.

components.name: DrillButton

props.name: children
props.description: Button label.

props.name: onDrill
props.description: Drill/navigation handler — wire to in-widget navigation (e.g. useHostActions().showWidget).

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional leading Lucide icon (decorative, never a typed glyph); the trailing Lucide arrow is always rendered.

props.name: size
props.description: 'sm' for table rows, 'md' for surface headers. Default 'sm'.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible label when the visible text is terse; keep the visible text in it (WCAG 2.5.3).

components.whenToUse: The single neutral in-widget navigation control (drill into a detail/sub-view). Use it for every drill so they read identically and stay visually quieter than primary/agentic actions.

components.name: ListFooter

props.name: shown
props.description: How many rows are currently rendered.

props.name: total
props.description: Total rows available. Renders nothing when 0.

props.name: hasMore
props.description: Whether a 'Load more' button is shown.

props.name: onLoadMore
props.description: Called when the user asks for the next page.

props.name: loadingMore
props.description: Disables the button + shows a loading label while a fetch is in flight.

props.name: noun
props.description: Plural noun for the count, e.g. 'instances'. Default: the locale's word for rows.

props.name: refreshing
props.description: A first page is in flight while these rows stay on screen: the status line adds a visible 'Updating…'.

props.name: stale
props.description: The rows on screen are the previous result: count and Load more hide, so the old count never reads as the new search's answer.

props.name: labels
props.description: Override strings of the active catalog's listFooter section.

props.name: announce
props.description: Make the count line a polite live region (role=status). Default true; false only where the caller announces the count in a live region of its own.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element.

components.whenToUse: Footer for a paginated list: an honest 'Showing X of Y' total + an explicit 'Load more' (not infinite scroll). The count is a polite live region (role=status), so the new total is announced after Load more or a filter change. At zero rows it shows nothing but keeps the region mounted (visually hidden) with 'No entries', so a search that finds nothing is announced too. Text and number format follow the active locale. For a paged query with failures use PagedListFooter.

components.name: PagedListFooter

props.name: paged
props.description: { items, total, hasMore, loadMore, loadingMore?, refreshing?, stale?, firstPage?, error?, retry?, loadMoreError? } — a paged-query hook's result passes as is.

props.name: noun
props.description: Plural noun for the count. Default: the locale's word for rows.

props.name: labels
props.description: Override strings of the active catalog's listFooter section.

props.name: retryLabel
props.description: Retry button label of both error lines. Default: the locale's 'Try again'.

components.whenToUse: The tail of a paged list: a failed first page over the previous rows (warning alert, retry re-runs page 0) and a failed load-more (danger alert, retry fetches the next offset) stay apart, each with the raw reason under Details; then the ListFooter with 'Updating…' while page 0 is in flight and no count while the rows are stale.

components.name: Tone tokens
components.whenToUse: Record<ToneVariant, string> maps from a status tone ('neutral'|'info'|'success'|'warning'|'danger') to Tailwind class strings, three roles per tone (Miragon CI): the colour for fills, dots, borders and icons (TONE_DOT, TONE_BORDER, TONE_ICON), the tint (TONE_SOFT = tint + foreground text, rim in the tone via TONE_BORDER; TONE_TINT = the tint alone; never put TONE_INK on a tint) and the TEXT colour for a tone's words on a plain surface (TONE_INK = the tone's -ink role; TONE_TEXT is its deprecated name). Status is never text in its own colour: success and warning ink is the foreground, so show the tone as a dot, icon or border next to the text; figures (counts, KPI values) stay in the foreground. TONE_ICON is for SVG icons only. Use to colour a custom element by status without a tone === 'x' ? ... ternary; the tone-aware components (KpiGrid, LivePill, CountPill, StatusBadge, Badge) consume these internally.

components.name: Tone vocabulary

props.name: name
props.description: A tone name, possibly from data: a ToneVariant or a retired alias ('critical', 'error', 'destructive', 'warn', 'ok', …).

props.name: fallback
props.description: The tone for anything unknown. Default 'neutral'.

components.whenToUse: ONE tone vocabulary: success | warning | danger | info | neutral (TONE_VARIANTS). resolveTone maps a retired or foreign name onto it (critical/error/destructive → danger; one red, one amber) and anything unknown onto the fallback, so a tone that arrives as data never renders colourless; isToneVariant is the type guard. The props typed ToneName resolve it this way (KpiCell tone/trendTone, LivePill, StatusBadge, CountPill, WidgetHeader iconTone). Toast, ErrorState and EmptyState keep their own tone subset in the types; an untyped name still resolves at runtime and anything outside the subset gets their default. Badge/Alert variants are cva keys: pass a resolved tone.

components.name: ToastProvider

props.name: children
props.description: Subtree that raises toasts via useToast.

components.whenToUse: Provide toasts to a subtree and render their stack: bottom centre, status colour as left edge + icon next to plain text, ONE persistent live region (aria-live=polite, fixed attributes: no role or name, so the first toast is announced; tests find it by data-slot=toast-viewport), toast text at 16 px, auto-dismiss after 2.8 s (errors 5 s), held while hovered or focused. Idempotent when nested. McpAppView mounts one, so widgets inside a view only call useToast. Toast icons follow the LucideProvider around the outermost ToastProvider (stroke 2.5 inside McpAppView).

components.name: useToast
components.whenToUse: Raise feedback after a user action instead of logging to the console: useToast().show({ tone: 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info', title, description?, duration? }) returns an id; dismiss(id) removes it early. Name the object in the title ('Job retried.'); the description says what to do next. Both come from your catalog: never put a raw error (e.message) in a toast, log it or show it under an ErrorState's Details. Outside a ToastProvider it is a safe no-op.

components.name: EmptyState

props.name: title
props.description: What is empty, in plain words.

props.name: description
props.description: One help line: why it is empty or what to do next.

props.name: icon
props.description: Decorative icon or brand mark (aria-hidden): a Lucide icon for the situation (24 px), or a logo; an SVG with its own size-* class keeps that size.

props.name: tone
props.description: Icon colour; 'success' for an 'all done' state. Default 'neutral'.

props.name: action
props.description: The primary next step (a Button).

props.name: secondaryAction
props.description: An optional second, quieter step (at most two actions).

props.name: titleAs
props.description: Title element. Default 'h3'.

components.whenToUse: The one empty-state pattern for a list, table or view with nothing to show: icon or mark, a 600-weight title, one help line, up to two actions. Static (no live region). Use instead of a grey one-liner; for 'all done' pass <CircleCheck /> with tone 'success'.

components.name: ErrorState

props.name: title
props.description: What happened, in plain words.

props.name: description
props.description: What you can do next (or the human reason).

props.name: details
props.description: The raw technical reason, shown collapsed under a 'Details' disclosure.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Renders a retry button (label from the locale) when set.

props.name: actions
props.description: Further actions after the retry button.

props.name: tone
props.description: Default 'danger'.

props.name: variant
props.description: 'block' replaces a view or widget body; 'inline' is an alert above content that still renders. Default 'block'.

props.name: role
props.description: Live-region role. Default 'alert'.

props.name: icon
props.description: Replace the tone's default Lucide icon.

props.name: titleAs
props.description: Title element. Default 'h2' (block) / 'p' (inline).

components.whenToUse: The one error pattern: icon, a title that says what happened, a line that says what you can do, the raw error under 'Details', and a retry. Never print a raw exception as the only text, never leave a failed fetch on an endless skeleton.

components.name: useDebouncedValue

props.name: value
props.description: The value to debounce.

props.name: delayMs
props.description: Debounce delay in ms. Default 300.

components.whenToUse: Debounce a search box (e.g. FilterBar's search) so a server-side filter only re-queries once the user pauses typing. Returns the value delayed by delayMs.

components.name: useToolQuery

props.name: queryKey
props.description: Cache key prefix. The effective key is [...queryKey, args] (toolQueryKey): different args get separate entries. Two tools must not share a key and args (the hook warns when they do), unless AppQueryProvider / McpAppView toolNameInQueryKey puts the tool name into the key ([...queryKey, toolName, args]).

props.name: toolName
props.description: MCP tool to call (e.g. a generated *_data feed).

props.name: args
props.description: Tool arguments.

props.name: opts
props.description: TanStack query options (retry, retryDelay, staleTime, placeholderData / keepPreviousData, initialData + initialDataUpdatedAt, enabled, select, gcTime, …) — everything but queryKey/queryFn. retry defaults to the client's; retry: shouldRetryToolCall stops retrying a tool's own isError answer.

components.whenToUse: Self-fetch arbitrary data from a tool inside a cockpit-embedded widget. Result is decoded with parseToolResult (structured-first). Returns a TanStack UseQueryResult (data, error, refetch, failureCount, failureReason, isFetching, isPlaceholderData, …). The tool goes through AppQueryProvider's callTool, else the nearest HostBridgeProvider; with neither the query fails with a 'no tool transport' error instead of idling. Keep a list on screen while a new search loads: { placeholderData: keepPreviousData }.

components.name: useToolMutation

props.name: toolName
props.description: MCP tool to invoke as the mutation.

props.name: opts
props.description: TanStack mutation options (onSuccess, onError, onSettled, retry, meta, mutationKey, …) plus invalidateKeys: query-key prefixes to invalidate after each successful call (active queries refetch, inactive ones turn stale).

components.whenToUse: Run a write/action tool (e.g. retry-incident) and invalidate dependent queries. Returns a TanStack UseMutationResult; call .mutate(args, { onSuccess, onError, onSettled }). Unlike TanStack's own mutate, the per-call callbacks fire for EVERY call while the widget is mounted, so two quick calls each get their confirmation.

components.name: toolQueryKey

props.name: queryKey
props.description: The caller's key prefix.

props.name: toolName
props.description: The tool the query calls.

props.name: args
props.description: The tool arguments.

props.name: toolNameInKey
props.description: Put the tool name between the key and the args ([...queryKey, toolName, args]). Default false (the 2.x key); the default from the next major.

components.whenToUse: Build the exact cache key useToolQuery / useViewToolQuery / useViewData use for getQueryData, setQueryData or cancelQueries with exact: true, never by hand. Pass toolNameInKey when the provider sets toolNameInQueryKey, or use useToolQueryKey, which reads it. Prefix invalidation needs only your queryKey.

components.name: useToolQueryKey

props.name: queryKey
props.description: The caller's key prefix, as passed to useToolQuery.

props.name: toolName
props.description: The tool the query calls.

props.name: args
props.description: The tool arguments.

components.whenToUse: The exact cache key the data hooks use for this tool and args under the nearest AppQueryProvider (toolQueryKey with its toolNameInQueryKey setting), for getQueryData, setQueryData or cancelQueries with exact: true, e.g. for an optimistic update in a mutation's onMutate. Stays right when the next major puts the tool name into every key.

components.name: shouldRetryToolCall

props.name: failureCount
props.description: Failed attempts so far.

props.name: error
props.description: The last failure.

components.whenToUse: An opt-in retry policy for tool queries: no retry for a tool's own isError answer (isToolError) or a missing transport, up to 3 retries for a failed transport, so a deterministic tool error shows at once instead of after ~7 s. Pass retry: shouldRetryToolCall to a hook, or set it as the client's default. The hooks keep the client's retry by default.

components.name: keepPreviousData
components.whenToUse: TanStack's placeholder helper, re-exported so no direct @tanstack/react-query import is needed: { placeholderData: keepPreviousData } keeps the previous args' answer on screen (isPlaceholderData: true) while a changed search or filter loads — a list never unmounts mid-typing.

components.name: useViewToolQuery

props.name: queryKey
props.description: Cache key prefix; the effective key is [...queryKey, args] (sibling widgets with equal args dedupe).

props.name: toolName
props.description: A *_show_* widget tool whose structuredContent is the full view envelope.

props.name: args
props.description: Tool arguments.

props.name: opts
props.description: TanStack query options (retry, retryDelay, staleTime, placeholderData / keepPreviousData, initialData + initialDataUpdatedAt, enabled, select, gcTime, …) — everything but queryKey/queryFn, as useToolQuery.

components.whenToUse: Self-fetch from a *_show_* widget tool. Unwraps the McpAppView view envelope via parseViewToolResult (single-step → flat data, multi-step → keyed by step id) — the envelope-aware sibling of useToolQuery.

components.name: useViewData

props.name: initialData
props.description: Host-pushed data (e.g. from adaptDataWidget). Returned verbatim by default; with initialDataMode 'seed' it becomes the feed query's cached answer.

props.name: key
props.description: Cache key for the fallback self-fetch.

props.name: tool
props.description: Tool to call when initialData is absent.

props.name: args
props.description: Tool arguments for the fallback fetch.

props.name: ready
props.description: Whether the required id/key is present; the feed stays off until ready (and, by default, while initialData is present).

props.name: options
props.description: TanStack query options (retry, retryDelay, staleTime, placeholderData / keepPreviousData, initialDataUpdatedAt, enabled, gcTime, …) — everything but queryKey/queryFn; enabled is an extra gate next to ready. initialDataMode: 'static' (default) or 'seed' — seed keeps the feed live over host data, so a write's invalidation, a refetch or a retry re-reads it.

components.whenToUse: The dual-mode seam: write ONE widget that renders host-pushed data when handed it (standalone *_show_* widget) AND self-fetches when embedded in a cockpit. Returns { data, loading, error, refetch, failureCount, failureReason, isFetching, isPlaceholderData }; pass refetch as the error state's retry (<ErrorState onRetry={refetch} />). Pass { initialDataMode: 'seed' } when a standalone view must stay live after writes, { placeholderData: keepPreviousData } to keep rows on screen while new args load.

components.name: useIsMobile
components.whenToUse: Switch a widget between compact and wide layouts below the 768px breakpoint. Returns boolean.

components.name: useHostBridge
components.whenToUse: THE host seam for portable widgets. Returns a HostBridge { callTool, sendFollowup, openExternal, getWidgetData, setModelContext?, theme? }. Use this instead of mcp-use/react or window.openai directly so the same widget runs in the mcp-use host, ChatGPT, or standalone. Requires a provider: McpToolkitApp (toolkit host), WidgetFixtureHost (dev), or an explicit HostBridgeProvider.

components.name: useHostActions
components.whenToUse: Named-affordance facade over useHostBridge: returns { openLink, showWidget, askAi }. Handy for in-widget navigation (showWidget) and handing open-ended tasks to the agent (askAi). New portable widgets can also use useHostBridge directly.

components.name: buildShowWidgetIntent

props.name: toolName
props.description: The *_show_* tool the agent should invoke.

props.name: description
props.description: Natural-language description of what to show.

components.whenToUse: Build the intent string for host.showWidget(...) — appends a '(use <toolName>)' hint so the agent picks the right tool unambiguously.

components.name: HostBridgeProvider

props.name: bridge
props.description: The explicit bridge to provide (createChatGptHostBridge / createStandaloneHostBridge, or toHostBridge over a custom surface).

props.name: children
props.description: Subtree whose useHostBridge() resolves to this bridge.

components.whenToUse: Wrap a portable widget in the bridge for the host it runs in. Inside the toolkit's own host you do not need it — McpToolkitApp installs the mcp-use bridge via McpUseHostBridgeProvider.

components.name: McpUseHostBridgeProvider

props.name: children
props.description: Subtree whose useHostBridge() resolves to the mcp-use bridge.

components.whenToUse: Composes the mcp-use 2.x view hooks into the HostBridge and provides it. Already included in McpToolkitApp — reach for it only when building a custom shell under your own bootstrapView call. Throws outside a bootstrapView-mounted view.

components.name: createStandaloneHostBridge

props.name: options
props.description: { callTool (required), getData?, onFollowup?, onOpenExternal?, onModelContext?, theme? }.

components.whenToUse: Build a HostBridge for a standalone web app against any MCP server (callTool usually wraps a @modelcontextprotocol/client client). The WidgetFixtureHost builds on this too.

components.name: createChatGptHostBridge

props.name: sdk
props.description: Explicit window.openai for testing; defaults to the real one.

components.whenToUse: Build a HostBridge mapping the bridge verbs onto the OpenAI Apps SDK (ChatGPT). Defensive — missing host methods degrade to logged no-ops.

components.name: adaptDataWidget

props.name: Widget
props.type: ComponentType<{ data: T | null } & Record<string, unknown>>
props.description: A single-data widget — write it as ({ data }) and it stays host-agnostic.

props.name: dataType
props.description: The step _dataType to pull data from in context.steps.

props.name: describeForModel
props.description: (data, props) => string. Wraps the widget in <HostModelContext> so the model knows what the user is looking at.

components.whenToUse: Register a hand-built ({ data }) widget as a framework WidgetComponent. The adapter finds the matching step in context.steps[_dataType].data and forwards result.data as the data prop, and spreads per-cell layout props. Lets render-view and *_show_* tools share one widget.

components.name: HostModelContext

props.name: content
props.description: The model-facing description of what the user is looking at (view identity, filters, headline numbers).

props.name: children
props.description: The widget subtree the description belongs to (nested below it). Omit it to report one line where it renders.

components.whenToUse: Report model context from a widget that self-fetches (cockpit views) — the host-portable replacement for mcp-use/react's ModelContext. Inside an mcp-use view it renders the native aggregating ModelContext; in every other mount (widget playground, ChatGPT, standalone) it routes through the HostBridge's setModelContext. NEVER import ModelContext from mcp-use/react in a widget: it throws outside a bootstrapView mount.

components.name: useHostModelContext

props.name: content
props.description: One line for the model; blank or null reports nothing.

components.whenToUse: Report one line of model context from a component with nothing to wrap (a selection, a filter, an error the user sees) for as long as it is mounted. Inside an mcp-use view the line joins the view's one model-context tree with every HostModelContext and leaves it on unmount; elsewhere it goes through the HostBridge's setModelContext.

components.name: DescribeForModel

props.name: (type)
props.description: The describeForModel callback signature for adaptDataWidget.

components.whenToUse: Type the model-context line builder you pass to adaptDataWidget — report view identity, active filters, and headline numbers so the agent has context on the next turn.

components.name: parseToolResult

props.name: result
props.description: The raw MCP tool result.

props.name: opts
props.description: Channel preference. Default 'structured' (structuredContent-first).

components.whenToUse: Decode a raw callTool result to its data payload. Structured-first: isError → throw, then structuredContent, then JSON-decoded text, then raw. useToolQuery decodes through this for you.

components.name: ToolResultError

props.name: message
props.description: The tool's first text block.

props.name: result
props.description: The isError result as the tool returned it.

components.whenToUse: The Error class parseToolResult throws for an isError result — a deterministic answer of the tool (validation error, engine 404), not a transport failure. The query hooks never retry it by default. Check with isToolError (also matches mcp-use's ToolError).

components.name: isToolError

props.name: error
props.description: Anything a tool call rejected with.

components.whenToUse: Tell a tool's own isError answer (ToolResultError, or mcp-use's ToolError inside a view) from a transport failure — e.g. in a custom retry policy or to word an error state.

components.name: parseViewToolResult

props.name: result
props.description: The raw result of a *_show_* widget tool.

components.whenToUse: Unwrap a *_show_* view envelope (context.stepData) to the flat widget data: single-step → that step's data; multi-step → object keyed by step id. Non-envelope results pass through parseToolResult.

components.name: cn

props.name: ...classes
props.description: clsx inputs.

components.whenToUse: Merge Tailwind class strings (clsx + tailwind-merge). Use for conditional/override classes; later conflicting utilities win.

components.name: createTheme

props.name: tokens
props.description: Brand tokens (all optional), one field per role of the role-token contract (ROLE_TOKENS): primary, primaryForeground, primaryHover, link, focus, ring, background, foreground, card, popover, muted, mutedForeground, secondary, accent, border, input, destructive, success/warning/danger/info with *Soft and *Ink, radiusSm/Md/Lg/Pill, shadow1-3, scrim, motionFast/Base/Slow, ease, fontSans, fontMono, plus the legacy accentForeground, cardForeground, radius, fontHeading. Colors are any CSS color string.

props.name: opts
props.description: Dark-mode token overrides. In dark mode a theme scope gets the toolkit's dark defaults, the theme's mode-invariant light tokens (brand button colour, radii, fonts) and these — never the other light values.

components.whenToUse: Define a white-label theme for a customer brand. The toolkit's default IS the Miragon theme (no theme needed for it). Maps the fields onto the role CSS variables (--primary, --link, --focus, ...) and returns a serializable ThemeDefinition { vars, darkVars?, toStyle() }. Apply it with ThemeProvider so every primitive re-skins; override roles only, never --cd-* tokens or component classes.

components.name: ThemeProvider

props.name: theme
props.description: The theme from createTheme to apply. Omit to manage only the light/dark mode against the toolkit defaults (the Miragon theme).

props.name: mode
props.description: Color-scheme mode. Default 'light'. Pass HostBridge.theme to follow the host, or 'system' to track prefers-color-scheme (SSR-safe).

props.name: as
props.description: Scope wrapper element. Default 'div'.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the scope wrapper.

props.name: children
props.description: Subtree that inherits the theme's CSS variables and dark class.

components.whenToUse: Wrap a widget (or a whole app) to apply a ThemeDefinition and/or a light/dark mode to a scope. Light mode applies the theme's vars, dark mode the toolkit's dark roles plus the theme's dark and mode-invariant tokens (resolveThemeVars). A light scope stays light inside a dark document. Dialogs, Sheets and Select menus opened inside portal into the scope, so they keep its theme and mode. React + DOM only — no host required.

components.name: useTheme
components.whenToUse: Read the active theme/mode from the nearest ThemeProvider. Returns { theme, mode, resolvedMode } where resolvedMode is 'system' resolved to 'light'|'dark'. Throws outside a ThemeProvider.

components.name: themePresets
components.whenToUse: Ready-made white-label themes — a demonstration of createTheme and a fork-able starting point (themePresets.emerald). themePresets.miragon and .violet are deprecated: the Miragon theme is the toolkit's default, use no theme for it. Pass a preset to ThemeProvider's theme prop.

components.name: resolveThemeVars

props.name: theme
props.description: The theme; null/undefined yields {}.

props.name: mode
props.description: The resolved mode of the scope.

components.whenToUse: The CSS variables a ThemeDefinition applies at its scope in a mode — what ThemeProvider puts on its wrapper. Use it to theme an element without ThemeProvider (spread it into style), e.g. resolveThemeVars(theme, host.theme ?? 'light'). A legacy base radius also derives the sm/md/lg steps.

components.name: ROLE_TOKENS
components.whenToUse: The role-token contract as a readonly list of CSS variable names (--background … --font-mono). Components style through these roles only; a brand overrides only these. Use it to check a brand stylesheet or a host token map covers / stays within the contract.

components.name: usePortalContainer
components.whenToUse: The portal node of the nearest ThemeProvider (or null). Pass it as `container` to a portal of your own so overlays keep the scope's theme and light/dark mode; the toolkit's Dialog, Sheet and Select already do.

components.name: CD_TOKENS
components.whenToUse: The Miragon corporate-design tokens (--cd-*) as plain TypeScript, keys without the prefix (CD_TOKENS.blau, CD_TOKENS['danger-soft']). For code that cannot read CSS variables — SVG/canvas renderers, chart marks, server-side images. Drift-tested against the vendored CSS. UI components style through the role tokens, never through these constants.

components.name: fontFaces

props.name: baseUrl
props.description: Where the woff2 files (GEIST_FONT_FILES) are served from.

props.name: files
props.description: File-name overrides.

props.name: display
props.description: Default 'swap'.

components.whenToUse: Opt-in Geist delivery by URL: returns the @font-face rules for Geist and Geist Mono (latin, variable weight) served from baseUrl. Inject into the view document, e.g. <style>{fontFaces({ baseUrl })}</style>, and allow that origin in the view CSP. Alternative: import @miragon/mcp-toolkit-ui/fonts.css (bundled). The font tokens name Geist first, so either path works; without either the host's font (see adoptHostFontVariables) or the system stack renders.

components.name: adoptHostFontVariables

props.name: style
props.description: The inline style the host variables were applied to, normally document.documentElement.style.

props.name: hostVariables
props.description: The host's SEP-1865 style variables (hostContext.styles.variables).

components.whenToUse: Keeps Geist first when a host sends its font. SEP-1865 hosts send --font-sans/--font-mono, the same names as the toolkit's font roles, and would replace the Geist-first stacks whole; this moves them to --host-font-sans/--host-font-mono, the fallback slot right after Geist. McpToolkitApp already calls it; call it yourself only in an app with its own host-document layer, right after applying the host's style variables.

components.name: FOCUS_RING
components.whenToUse: The kit's opaque focus ring as a class string (2px ring in --focus with an offset; FOCUS_RING_INSET draws it inside, for cells flush with a container edge). Spread it into a custom control's className so keyboard focus reads the same everywhere (3:1 or more in both modes).

components.name: Type scale
components.whenToUse: The CI type scale as role tokens and utilities: text-title (28/700, page title), text-section (21/600), text-body (16/400/1.6, running text incl. state and toast descriptions), text-dense (14, dense tables and controls such as inputs, chips, count pills and the inline alert box; never running text), text-small (13, the floor: captions, hints, meta rows). Nothing renders below 13 px: no text-xs, no text-[10px]; a former 10–11 px uppercase caption is MICRO_LABEL (13 px semibold, normal case). Combine with the kit's cn (plain tailwind-merge drops text-small next to a text colour). Brands resize via --text-* (ThemeTokens textTitle … textSmall).

components.name: LocaleProvider

props.name: locale
props.description: The active locale tag (e.g. 'en', 'de'). Resolve it on the host/server (header, user profile, session store) and pass it in.

props.name: translator
props.description: A translator from createTranslator(catalogs) (@miragon/mcp-toolkit-core). Omit to provide the locale only (useTranslate echoes keys).

props.name: toolkitMessages
props.description: Override individual toolkit strings per catalog section (e.g. { listFooter: { loadMore: 'Show more' } }). Omitted entries keep the shipped en/de catalog of locale.

props.name: children
props.description: Subtree whose widgets read the locale via useLocale/useTranslate.

components.whenToUse: Wrap a widget (or a whole app) to provide the active locale + an optional translator. Widgets read it with useLocale/useTranslate. Pure React (no host required), mirroring ThemeProvider — pairs with createTranslator from @miragon/mcp-toolkit-core. The toolkit's own components read their strings from it too (en/de, English otherwise), so passing the locale localizes the whole toolkit chrome.

components.name: useLocale
components.whenToUse: Read the active locale tag (e.g. 'de') from the nearest LocaleProvider. Returns 'en' outside a provider (does not throw), so unwrapped widgets keep rendering.

components.name: useTranslate
components.whenToUse: Get a locale-bound translate (key, params?) => string from the nearest LocaleProvider. Outside a provider it echoes the key, so a missing wrapper degrades gracefully instead of crashing.

components.name: useToolkitMessages
components.whenToUse: Read the toolkit's own UI strings (common, view, listFooter, filterBar, pills, renderer, builder, propsSheet) for the nearest LocaleProvider's locale: the shipped en/de catalog, English for any other locale, with the provider's toolkitMessages override applied. Reuse them in a widget for consistent chrome copy (e.g. common.retry).

components.name: TOOLKIT_MESSAGES
components.whenToUse: The shipped toolkit catalogs keyed by locale ({ en, de }), typed as ToolkitMessages. Use it to build a LocaleProvider toolkitMessages override or to assert in a consumer test that no toolkit default leaks into a localized bundle.

components.name: resolveToolkitMessages

props.name: locale
props.description: Any BCP 47 tag; its primary language picks the catalog (en fallback).

props.name: override
props.description: Per-section partial override merged over the catalog.

components.whenToUse: Resolve the toolkit catalog outside React (the pure function behind LocaleProvider/useToolkitMessages).

components.name: formatCount

props.name: value
props.description: The count.

props.name: locale
props.description: The app locale (from useLocale), not the browser's.

components.whenToUse: Format a count with the app locale's grouping (1,234 / 1.234); an invalid tag falls back to English instead of throwing in render.

components.name: McpToolkitApp

props.name: widgets
props.description: Host-bundled widget registry keyed by widget id.

props.name: refreshToolName
props.description: Tool the refresh button invokes. Default 'refresh-view'.

props.name: labels
props.description: Override UI strings (loading, refresh, fullscreen).

components.whenToUse: The consumer root for the widget bundle — mount it with mountMcpToolkitApp, which wraps mcp-use's bootstrapView (ext-apps handshake, error boundary, auto-resize). Composes ThemeProvider and McpUseHostBridgeProvider around McpAppView. You usually do NOT write this when authoring a single widget; you register the widget in its widgets map.

components.name: mountMcpToolkitApp

props.name: props
props.description: Same props as McpToolkitApp (widgets, refreshToolName?, builderEnabled?, labels?).

components.whenToUse: The bundle entry point since mcp-use 2.x: mounts McpToolkitApp via bootstrapView (ext-apps handshake, error boundary, auto-resize). Call it once in main.tsx instead of createRoot().render().

components.name: installToolResultObserver
components.whenToUse: Only for a custom shell under its own bootstrapView: call it before bootstrapView so McpAppView can tell a stripped tool result (claude.ai) from a slow tool and never re-runs a call the host is still answering. mountMcpToolkitApp and the bundle's first evaluation install it already; idempotent, null outside a framed browser document.

components.name: WidgetFixtureHost

props.name: widget
props.description: The widget component under development.

props.name: data
props.description: Fixture data: keys map for ({ keys }) widgets, forwarded as data for ({ data }) widgets.

props.name: dataType
props.description: For adaptDataWidget components: seeds a pipeline step whose _dataType matches so the adapter resolves data.

props.name: tools
props.description: Tool fixtures keyed by tool name. A static value or a (args) => result handler. Drives useToolQuery and callTool.

props.name: globals
props.description: Host-context overrides (theme, displayMode, locale...).

props.name: onModelContext
props.description: Receives the serialized <ModelContext> the widget reports — see what the model would see.

props.name: onHostAction
props.description: Receives every host action (tool call, link, follow-up).

components.whenToUse: Storybook-style harness: render ONE widget with fixture data and a simulated HostBridge (no backend, no real host). This is the prompt → see → iterate loop; add a Story to examples/widget-playground/stories.ts.

components.name: buildFixtureWidgetProps

props.name: data
props.description: Fixture data used as keys map and (when dataType set) the seeded step's data.

props.name: dataType
props.description: Seed the single pipeline step under this _dataType for adaptDataWidget components.

components.whenToUse: Build the WidgetProps envelope the fixture host passes to a widget — exported mainly for unit testing the envelope shape without rendering React.
